STATUTORY INSTRUMENTS

S.I. No. 229 of 2005

National Monuments Act, 1930 (Section 14B) Regulations, 2005

S.I. No. 229 2005

National Monuments Act, 1930 (Section 14B) Regulations, 2005.

The Minister for the Environment, Heritage and Local Government, in exercise of the powers conferred on him by Section 14B(11) of the National Monuments Act, 1930 (No. 2 of 1930), (as inserted by Section 5 of the National Monuments (Amendment Act, 2004 (No. 22 of 2004)), hereby makes the following Regulations:

1.   These Regulations may be cited as the National Monuments Act, 1930 (Section 14B) Regulations, 2004.

2.   For the purposes of these Regulations, a reference to section 14B or to a provision of that section shall be read as a reference to section 14B of the National Monuments Act, 1930 as inserted by section 5 of the National Monuments (Amendment) Act, 2004.

3.   For the purposes of paragraph (c) of section 14B(7) the prescribed bodies or persons are listed in Schedule A to these Regulations.

4.   The prescribed forms for the purposes of section 14B(7) are set out in Schedule B to these Regulations as follows:

(a)  Form No. 1 or a form substantially to the like effect shall be the prescribed form for the purposes of paragraph (b) of section 14B(7).

(b)  Form No. 2 or a form substantially to the like effect shall be the prescribed form for the purposes of paragraph (c) of section 14B(7).

(c)  Form No. 3 or a form substantially to the like effect shall be the prescribed form for the purposes of paragraph (d) of section 14B(7).

SCHEDULE A

The prescribed bodies or persons for the purposes of Article 3 of these Regulations shall be:

(a)  The Minister for the Environment, Heritage and Local Government (where it appears to the road authority that the proposed change to the approved road development might have significant effects in relation to the architectural or archaeological heritage or to nature conservation).

(b)  Road Authorities adjacent to the area in which the proposed road development is located,

(c)  The Heritage Council,

(d)  An Taisce — The National Trust for Ireland and

(e)  Fáilte Ireland

An Bord Pleanála is an independent statutory body operating largely under the Planning and Development Acts and under various other statutes. Amongst its functions it is responsible for approving local authority infrastructure projects including motorways and certain roads under the Roads Acts. An Bord Pleanála, in exercising its functions, must have regard to any submissions which are received within the time specified.

EXPLANATORY NOTE

(This note is not part of the Instrument and does not purport to be a legal interpretation)

These Regulations prescribe the forms of notice to be used by a road authority and the bodies or persons to be notified by it pursuant to section 14B(7) of the National Monuments Act 1930 (as amended).

1 Insert the name of the road authority responsible for submitting the EIS to An Bord Pleanála. Where the road authority is acting for another road authority, under an agreement pursuant to the Local Government Act, 2001 or otherwise, the name of that road authority should also be given and an appropriate statement included.

2 Insert the location and a brief description of the proposed change to the approved road development

3 Insert the name of the approved road development

4 Insert Location. A copy of the EIS must be displayed in at least one location but there is no restriction on the number of locations.

5 Insert time and dates. The EIS must be displayed for at least one month.

6 Insert the name of the road authority responsible for submitting the EIS to An Bord Pleanála

7 Insert amount. The specified charge must not exceed the reasonable cost of making the copy.

8 Insert amount. The specified charge must not exceed the reasonable cost of making the copy.

9 Current Address of the Board

10 Insert date. The deadline must be not less than 28 days after the date of publication of this notice

1 Insert the name and address of the body or person prescribed in Schedule B of these Regulations

2 Insert the name of the Road Authority. Where the road authority is acting for another road authority under an agreement pursuant to the Local Government Act, 2001 or otherwise, the name of that road authority should also be given and an appropriate statement included.

3 Insert the location and a brief description of the proposed change to the approved road development

4 Insert the name of the approved road development.

5 Current address of the Board

6 Insert the specified date by which submissions must be made to An Bord Pleanála. This date must be the same as that published in the newspaper notice.

7 Insert details of the relevant official at the road authority

8 In the case of a county/city council the notice should be signed by the appropriate Director of Services or other senior official.
